metadata.title: 1975 Case 50
metadata.original_presentation: A seven-week-old girl was admitted to the hospital for cardiac catheterization. She was born at full term after an uneventful primiparous pregnancy. Cyanosis and a heart murmur were noted at birth.

required.content: What is the birth history and initial findings of the patient?
required.response: The patient was born at full term after an uneventful primiparous pregnancy with a birth weight of 2.7 kg. Cyanosis and a heart murmur were noted at birth.

teaching_points.content: Cyanosis and heart murmur at birth can indicate congenital heart defects.

required.content: What was the neonatal course and any treatments given?
required.response: Icterus was observed on the third day of life; phototherapy was administered for 10 days. The child was discharged after two weeks in the nursery.

teaching_points.content: Phototherapy is a common treatment for neonatal jaundice.

required.content: What is the family and perinatal history?
required.response: The mother had not used drugs and recalled no infections in the perinatal period; there was no family history of cardiac or hepatic disease.

teaching_points.content: Family history and maternal health can provide clues to congenital conditions.

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Congenital Heart Disease (e.g., Tetralogy of Fallot, Transposition of the Great Arteries)
Neonatal Jaundice
key_features: icterus on third day of life
supporting_evidence: icterus observed on the third day of life
refuting_evidence: discharged after two weeks, suggesting resolution

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Persistent Pulmonary Hypertension of the Newborn (PPHN)

required.content: What were the findings on physical examination during the first admission?
required.response: The patient was an irritable, jaundiced baby with mild cyanosis of the lips at rest. The heart was not enlarged; there was a prominent right ventricular impulse and a Grade 3 holosystolic murmur.

teaching_points.content: A holosystolic murmur can indicate a ventricular septal defect or other cardiac anomalies.

required.content: What were the findings on physical examination during the second admission?
required.response: The child was icteric with acral cyanosis, alert and playful. The abdomen was distended, the liver was firm and extended 4 cm below the right costal margin.

teaching_points.content: Hepatomegaly and jaundice in infants can be signs of liver dysfunction or biliary atresia.

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Congenital Heart Disease (e.g., Tetralogy of Fallot)
supporting_evidence: cyanosis and heart murmur noted at birth

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Neonatal Jaundice (e.g., due to Hemolytic Disease or Liver Dysfunction)
supporting_evidence: icterus observed on the third day of life
liver firm and extended 4 cm below the right costal margin
refuting_evidence: no family history of hepatic disease

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Biliary Atresia
supporting_evidence: liver firm and extended 4 cm below the right costal margin
refuting_evidence: no specific mention of acholic stools

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Congenital Heart Disease with Hepatic Congestion
supporting_evidence: cyanosis and heart murmur noted at birth
liver firm and extended 4 cm below the right costal margin

required.content: What were the key laboratory findings?
required.response: The conjugated bilirubin was elevated, SGOT was high, and the 5′ nucleotidase was elevated. The urine was dark with a positive test for bilirubin.

teaching_points.content: Elevated conjugated bilirubin and liver enzymes suggest cholestasis or liver dysfunction.

required.content: What were the imaging and biopsy findings?
required.response: Chest x-ray showed right ventricular enlargement. Liver biopsy revealed moderate cholestasis and giant-cell transformation.

teaching_points.content: Liver biopsy can help diagnose the cause of jaundice and liver dysfunction.

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Congenital Heart Disease (e.g., Tetralogy of Fallot)
supporting_evidence: cyanosis and heart murmur noted at birth
right ventricular enlargement on chest x-ray
additional_information_needed: Echocardiogram to assess cardiac anatomy and function

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Biliary Atresia
additional_information_needed: Hepatobiliary scintigraphy to assess bile flow

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Neonatal Hepatitis
additional_information_needed: Viral serologies to rule out infectious causes

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Alagille Syndrome
refuting_evidence: no mention of facial dysmorphism or vertebral anomalies

required.content: What treatments were initiated during the hospital stay?
required.response: Cholestyramine was begun, and cardiac catheterization was cancelled.

teaching_points.content: Cholestyramine is used to treat pruritus associated with cholestasis.

final_diagnosis.name: Congenital heart defect with associated liver dysfunction
